nad18bc0c90b.s:
Consider the following statements about paragraph 386 of the SRC report:
1. The departure from paragraph 386 remained a core grievance of later Telangana movements.
2. This grievance figured in the Telangana movements of 1969 and 2001-14.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nad18bc0c90b.x: Both are correct: the departure from paragraph 386 was a central grievance in the Telangana movements of 1969 and 2001-14.

n0104e36b2e8.s:
Consider the following statements about the SRC's review mechanism for Telangana (para 386):
1. Unification with Andhra could come only after 1961.
2. It needed the support of two-thirds of the elected members of the Telangana Assembly.
3. It needed the support of three-fourths of the elected members of the Telangana Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n0104e36b2e8.x: Unification after 1961 needed two-thirds of the elected Telangana members, not three-fourths, so statement 3 is wrong.

n35bf9d744b2.s: Paragraph 386 of the States Reorganisation Commission report recommended that Telangana should initially:
o: Function as a separate state called Hyderabad State
Become a Union Territory under the Centre
n35bf9d744b2.x: Paragraph 386 recommended that Telangana initially function as a separate state to be called Hyderabad State.

n1e9f7d06aab.s: In which year was the second Visalandhra Mahasabha held at Hyderabad?
n1e9f7d06aab.x: The second Mahasabha met at Hyderabad in June 1954, after the founding (1949), the Warangal session (1950) and the APCC Kurnool resolution (1953).

nea85fa7eb21.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, at least how many of the portfolios of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, and Commerce and Industry were to go to Telangana?
nea85fa7eb21.x: At least two of these five portfolios were to go to Telangana.

nf3ea434286f.s: How many seats did the Telugu Desam Party win in the 1983 Andhra Pradesh Assembly election?
nf3ea434286f.x: The TDP won 202 seats in 1983 and formed the first non-Congress government in AP.

n3fd368dfa08.s: Which of the following about the 1984 political crisis in Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
o: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao was sworn in as Chief Minister on 16 August 1984
Indira Gandhi was assassinated on 31 October 1984
The mid-term polls were held before Indira Gandhi's assassination
N.T. Rama Rao was sworn in again on 9 March 1985
n3fd368dfa08.x: The mid-term polls were held on 28 December 1984, after Indira Gandhi's assassination on 31 October.

na1c44a23697.s: In 1956, the 11 districts of Andhra State were merged with how many Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State?
na1c44a23697.x: The 11 Andhra districts merged with nine Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State.

n1834c9e1a56.s: In which year did Swami Sitaram undertake his fast for the Andhra cause?
n1834c9e1a56.x: Swami Sitaram's fast came in 1951, after the Dhar Commission (1948) and the Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949), and before Andhra State (1953).

n0df238ceb71.s:
Consider the following statements about the formation of states:
1. Gujarat was formed in 1960.
2. Nagaland was formed in 1963.
3. Himachal Pradesh became a state in 1966.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n0df238ceb71.x: Gujarat (1960) and Nagaland (1963) are right; Himachal Pradesh became a state in 1971, not 1966.

nefe713ce155.s: Which of the following about the apportionment ratio under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is NOT correct?
o: The larger share went to Andhra Pradesh
The ratio was based on the 2011 Census population
Assets and liabilities were split equally, 50 : 50
nefe713ce155.x: The broad population ratio was 58.32:41.68 (AP:Telangana), from the 2011 Census, not an equal 50:50 split.

new.s: How many Zonal Councils were set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
new.x: Five Zonal Councils were set up: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern.

new.s: Who is the Chairman of every Zonal Council?
o: A member-state Chief Minister by annual rotation
new.x: The Union Home Minister chairs all Zonal Councils; a member-state CM is Vice-Chairman by annual rotation.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Zonal Councils:
1. They are statutory bodies set up under Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
2. Each state is represented by its Chief Minister and two ministers.
3. The Union Home Minister is the Vice-Chairman.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Union Home Minister is the Chairman; the Vice-Chairman is a member-state CM by rotation.

new.s: The main purpose of the Zonal Councils is:
new.x: Zonal Councils were created to promote inter-state cooperation.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended which Section of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 to read "Andhra Pradesh and Telangana"?
new.x: APRA 2014 amended Section 15 of the SR Act, 1956.

new.s: The States Reorganisation Commission submitted its report on:
new.x: The report was submitted on 30 September 1955 and made public on 9 October 1955.

new.s: About how many memorandums did the States Reorganisation Commission receive?
new.x: The SRC received 1,52,250 memorandums.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (region – SRC recommendation) is correctly matched?
o: Bombay – Split into Gujarat and Maharashtra
Telugu districts of Hyderabad – Immediate merger with Andhra
new.x: The SRC recommended a separate Vidarbha; Bombay was to be bilingual, Punjabi Suba was not accepted and the Telugu districts were to form a separate Hyderabad State.

new.s: The S.K. Dhar Commission (1948) preferred reorganisation of provinces on the basis of:
new.x: The Dhar Commission saw linguistic states as a threat to unity and preferred administrative convenience.

new.s: Who chaired the Madras Partition Committee of 1949–50?
new.x: The 1949–50 Partition Committee was chaired by Madras CM P.S. Kumaraswami Raja; the 1953 one was appointed by Rajagopalachari.

new.s: The 1953 Partition Committee appointed by C. Rajagopalachari consisted of:
o: Ministers and others under Kumaraswami Raja
new.x: Rajagopalachari's 1953 Partition Committee had members of his Cabinet only.

new.s: Justice K.N. Wanchoo, who inquired into the separation of Andhra in 1953, was then Chief Justice of which High Court?
new.x: Justice K.N. Wanchoo was Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court.

new.s: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after fasting for how many days?
new.x: Potti Sriramulu fasted from 19 October 1952 and died after 58 days.

new.s: Nehru announced the formation of Andhra State on:
new.x: After Sriramulu's death (15 Dec 1952) and the unrest, Nehru announced Andhra State on 19 December 1952.

new.s: Kurnool was chosen as the capital of Andhra State over Vijayawada by an Assembly vote of:
new.x: The Assembly chose Kurnool over Vijayawada by 80 votes to 79.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT an argument against linguistic states?
new.x: Government in the people's language was an argument for linguistic states; the others were arguments against.

new.s: Which was the first province formed on linguistic lines?
new.x: Orissa (1936) was the first linguistic province; Andhra (1953) was the first linguistic state of independent India.

new.s: Who moved the linguistic reorganisation resolution in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1918?
new.x: B.N. Sharma moved the resolution in 1918.

new.s: The first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha (1930) was held at:
new.x: The first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha met at Jogipet in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy.

new.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission?
new.x: The SRC had Fazl Ali, Kunzru and Panikkar; Tej Bahadur Sapru was not a member.

new.s: When appointed chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission, Syed Fazl Ali was the Governor of:
new.x: Syed Fazl Ali was Governor of Odisha.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a principle of reorganisation accepted by the SRC?
o: One language, one state as the only rule
new.x: The SRC rejected 'one language, one state'; language was important but not the only factor.

new.s: Which chapter of the SRC report dealt with Hyderabad?
new.x: Chapter 5 dealt with Hyderabad and Chapter 6 with Andhra.

new.s: Under the SRC scheme, Raichur and Gulbarga were to go to:
new.x: Raichur and Gulbarga were to go to Mysore; Marathwada to Bombay.

new.s: Which of the following was an argument for Visalandhra in paras 369–374 of the SRC report?
o: Telangana's revenue surplus would be diverted
Mulki rules would be at risk
Hyderabad would solve Andhra's capital problem
new.x: The capital argument favoured Visalandhra; the other three were arguments against immediate merger.

new.s: In 1955, whose resolution assuring Telangana priority and population-based shares was passed unanimously by the Andhra Assembly?
new.x: Andhra CM Bezawada Gopala Reddy's resolution was passed unanimously in 1955.

new.s: Who worked to allay Telangana's fears about the merger on the Congress High Command's direction?
new.x: Hyderabad CM Burgula Ramakrishna Rao worked to allay Telangana's fears.

new.s: In the Hyderabad Assembly vote on Visalandhra, how many members remained neutral?
new.x: The vote was 103 for, 29 against and 15 neutral.

new.s: On 22 October 1955, the Chief Ministers of Andhra and Hyderabad agreed to merge at:
new.x: The two CMs agreed to merge at Hyderabad House, Delhi, on 22 October 1955.

new.s: The Seventh Constitutional Amendment, 1956 replaced the Part A/B/C/D classification with:
o: Part A and Part B states only
new.x: The 7th Amendment abolished Part A/B/C/D and created states and Union Territories.

new.s: Article 350B, inserted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment, provides for:
o: Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
A Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
new.x: Art 350B provides a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities; Art 350A deals with mother-tongue instruction.

new.s: Bilingual Bombay was split into Gujarat and Maharashtra on:
new.x: Bombay was split on 1 May 1960.

new.s: The Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 followed the report of which commission?
new.x: The Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 came after the Shah Commission; Haryana was formed from 1 November 1966.

new.s: Who proposed one rule for all Telugu areas at the second Andhra Mahasabha in 1914?
new.x: Nyapati Subbarao made the proposal at the 1914 Mahasabha.

new.s: In 1954, who said the Visalandhra idea was 50 years old, as old as the Andhra Movement?
new.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao said so in 1954.

new.s: The Andhra Congress Swaraj Party manifesto, a root of the Visalandhra idea, came in:
new.x: The Swaraj Party manifesto came in 1936.

new.s: During the 1952 Mulki agitation, police firing killed students near:
new.x: The firing of 3–4 September 1952 was near City College, Hyderabad.

new.s: Who headed the inquiry commission into the 1952 City College firing?
new.x: Justice Pingali Jaganmohan Reddy reported on 28 December 1952.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mulki rules of Hyderabad State:
1. They were made stricter by the Nizam's farman of 1919.
2. Only residents of about 15 years got local jobs.
3. The 1952 inquiry led to a major change in the Mulki rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 3 is wrong: no major change in the Mulki rules followed the 1952 inquiry.

new.s: Who was the Speaker of the Hyderabad Assembly at the time of the merger?
new.x: Kashinatha Rao was the Speaker at the merger.

new.s: Hyderabad State was integrated with India on 17 September 1948 through:
new.x: Hyderabad was integrated through Operation Polo.

new.s: Who presided over the second Visalandhra Mahasabha at Hyderabad in June 1954?
new.x: Sri Sri presided in 1954; Hayagreevachari presided over the 1950 Warangal session.

new.s: In June 1953, the Hyderabad Congress proposed splitting Hyderabad State into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and:
new.x: The three-way split was Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and United Karnataka; it was rejected in 1954.

new.s: On 8 July 1954, a Hyderabad PCC delegation asked the SRC for:
o: A self-sufficient Telangana of 9 districts with Bastar and parts of Chanda
new.x: The delegation (Heda, J.V. Narsing Rao, Arige Ramaswamy) sought a self-sufficient Telangana.

new.s: Who backed a separate Telangana at the Telangana convention of November 1955?
new.x: Harishchandra Heda backed separate Telangana at the November 1955 convention.

new.s: The APCC resolution of January 1950 proposed Hyderabad as the permanent capital and ____ as the temporary capital.
new.x: The January 1950 APCC resolution: Madras temporary, Hyderabad permanent capital.

new.s: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao raised Visalandhra at the 1951 Congress manifesto meeting held at:
new.x: He raised it at Bangalore in 1951 and resigned when no decision came.

new.s: The People's Democratic Front (1952) in Hyderabad State was the electoral front of the:
new.x: The PDF was the Communists' electoral front in 1952, not the Congress's.

new.s: Which party in Hyderabad, under Mahadev Singh, opposed Visalandhra and wanted a separate Telangana?
new.x: The Hyderabad PSP under Mahadev Singh stood for a separate Telangana.

new.s: The paper 'Imroz' was associated with:
new.x: Imroz was Shoebullah Khan's; Rayyat was Mandumula Narsing Rao's.

new.s: The Communist daily 'Visalandhra' was started in:
new.x: The Visalandhra daily began in June 1952 at Sundarayya's initiative.

new.s: Who among the following was NOT a Communist leader of the Visalandhra campaign in Telangana?
new.x: Marri Chenna Reddy opposed Visalandhra throughout; the others were Communist leaders.

new.s: Who wrote 'Emaanandam ... Eenadu'?
new.x: Kaloji wrote it; Dasarathi wrote 'Enni Naalla Swapnamidi'.

new.s: Which leader backed Visalandhra but turned against it after becoming Telangana Congress president?
new.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy changed sides; Marri Chenna Reddy opposed throughout.

new.s: Which leader opposed Visalandhra throughout?
new.x: Marri Chenna Reddy was against throughout; Ranga Reddy and Kaloji changed their stands.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about leaders in the Visalandhra debate:
1. Kaloji supported Visalandhra and later opposed it.
2. Marri Chenna Reddy changed sides after becoming Telangana Congress president.
3. Makhdoom Mohiuddin was among the educated Muslims who supported it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 2 is wrong: it was K.V. Ranga Reddy who changed sides; Chenna Reddy opposed throughout.

new.s: Which of the following was a Telangana apprehension about the merger?
o: Telangana's revenue surplus being spent elsewhere
new.x: Diversion of the revenue surplus was a Telangana fear; the others were arguments for Visalandhra.

new.s: The river-waters argument for Visalandhra rested on integrated planning of the:
new.x: Integrated Krishna–Godavari planning was the river-waters argument.

new.s: In which year did the Andhra Assembly unanimously pass Bezawada Gopala Reddy's resolution on merger?
new.x: The resolution, giving Telangana priority and population-based shares, was passed in 1955.

new.s: In the Hyderabad Assembly vote on Visalandhra, how many members voted against?
new.x: The vote was 103 for, 29 against and 15 neutral.

new.s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra State after the 1955 mid-term polls?
new.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy became CM in 1955; he was the last CM of Andhra State.

new.s: Gouthu Latchanna signed the Gentlemen's Agreement as:
new.x: Gouthu Latchanna signed as a Minister from Andhra.

new.s: Who signed the Gentlemen's Agreement as President of the Hyderabad PCC?
new.x: J.V. Narsing Rao signed as Hyderabad PCC President; Alluri Satyanarayana Raju was APCC President.

new.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, the sale of agricultural land in Telangana was to be controlled by the:
new.x: Sale of agricultural land was to be controlled by the Regional Council.

new.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister were to be:
new.x: The CM and Deputy CM were to come from different regions.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement?
o: Prohibition in Telangana left to Telangana legislators
Cabinet seats shared 3:1 between Andhra and Telangana
Recruitment to services by population ratio
new.x: The cabinet ratio was 60:40, not 3:1.

new.s: The Telangana Regional Committee was wound up after the:
new.x: It was extended five years in 1968 and wound up after the 32nd Amendment, 1973.

new.s: Which of the following about the Telangana Regional Committee is NOT correct?
o: The Chief Minister was an ex officio member
Its members included Telangana MLAs and MPs elected by Telangana legislators
Telangana ministers were ex officio members
Its powers covered irrigation, education and recruitment
new.x: Telangana ministers except the CM were ex officio members.

new.s: Who was the first Deputy Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
new.x: Kalluri Subbarao was the first Deputy Speaker; Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, constituted in 1958, had how many members?
new.x: The Council was constituted in 1958 with 90 members.

new.s: The High Court at Hyderabad for Andhra Pradesh began functioning from:
new.x: The High Court functioned at Hyderabad from 5 November 1956.

new.s: After serving as the first Governor of Kerala, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao became Governor of:
new.x: Burgula became first Governor of Kerala (1956), then of Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: Which name did the Communists propose for the new state in 1956?
new.x: The draft Bill proposed 'Andhra Telangana', the Communists 'Visalandhra'; the final name was 'Andhra Pradesh'.

new.s: Which of the following was a reason for choosing Hyderabad as the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The SRC's view and the Mahasabha demand
The Kurnool Assembly vote of 80 to 79
new.x: Hyderabad was chosen on the SRC's view and the Visalandhra Mahasabha's demand.

new.s: With 40 members from Hyderabad and 119 from Andhra, the Congress strength in the new AP Assembly was:
new.x: 40 + 119 = 159 Congress members.

new.s: Who was the first Dalit Chief Minister in India?
new.x: Damodaram Sanjivayya, CM of AP from 11 January 1960, was the first Dalit CM in India.

new.s: Who had the longest continuous tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Chandrababu Naidu (1995–2004) had the longest continuous tenure.

new.s: In which year did Neelam Sanjiva Reddy become President of India?
new.x: He became President in 1977; in 1960 he was AICC President.

new.s: In 1984, Nadendla Bhaskara Rao formed the:
new.x: Nadendla formed the Democratic Telugu Desam Party; Chenna Reddy formed the National Democratic Party.

new.s: Which state introduced Panchayat Raj on 2 October 1959, before Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Rajasthan was first (2 Oct 1959); AP followed on 1 Nov 1959.

new.s: How many seats did the Congress win in the 1962 Andhra Pradesh Assembly election?
new.x: The Congress won 177 seats in 1962; the Communists won over 50.

new.s: Who was the last Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: N. Kiran Kumar Reddy (2010–14) was the last CM of united AP.

new.s: N.T. Rama Rao's Rs 2 per kg rice scheme began on:
new.x: The Rs 2/kg rice scheme began on 14 April 1983.

new.s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately after Damodaram Sanjivayya?
new.x: Sanjiva Reddy returned as CM (1962–64) after Sanjivayya.

new.s: After the Congress (I) was formed on 1 January 1978, who led the rival Reddy Congress?
new.x: Brahmananda Reddy led the Reddy Congress.

new.s: The Congress ruled Andhra Pradesh uninterruptedly during:
new.x: The Congress ruled without a break from 1956 to 1983.

new.s: Under Article 4, a law made under Article 3 is:
o: An amendment needing a special majority
An amendment needing ratification by half the states
Valid only after the state legislature consents
new.x: Article 4 says such a law is not an amendment under Article 368.

new.s: A Bill under Article 3 is passed by Parliament by a:
new.x: An Article 3 Bill is passed by a simple majority.

new.s: The admission or establishment of new states from outside India falls under:
new.x: Article 2 covers states from outside India (e.g. Sikkim); Article 3 covers reorganisation of existing states.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Article 3 procedure:
1. The views of the affected state legislature are binding on Parliament.
2. No reference is needed for a Union Territory.
3. A fresh reference is not needed for each amendment to the Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the state legislature's views are not binding.

new.s: Sikkim became a state of India in 1975 through the:
new.x: Sikkim became a state by the 36th Amendment (1975), not a 1987 Act.

new.s: Himachal Pradesh became a full state on:
new.x: HP became a state on 25 January 1971; in 1966 it only received Punjab's hill areas.

new.s: Which states were formed in 1987?
new.x: Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Goa became states in 1987.

new.s: Nagaland, the first North-Eastern state with full statehood, was carved out of:
new.x: Nagaland was carved out of Assam (State of Nagaland Act, 1962; statehood 1963).

new.s: The J&K Reorganisation of 2019 followed a presidential order under which Article that revoked the state's special status?
new.x: Special status was revoked by a presidential order under Article 370; two UTs came into being on 31 Oct 2019.

new.s: The 'Greater Rayalaseema' demand raised during the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh was:
o: Referred to the Srikrishna Committee for a new state
new.x: The Greater Rayalaseema demand was not accepted.

new.s: Of the three states formed in November 2000, which was formed first?
new.x: Chhattisgarh (1 Nov), Uttarakhand (9 Nov), Jharkhand (15 Nov).

new.s: The Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act was passed in:
new.x: The 1957 Act set a residence condition for Telangana posts.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Girglani Commission
2. GO 610
3. Jai Andhra movement
4. Six-Point Formula
new.x: Jai Andhra (1972) → Six-Point Formula (1973) → GO 610 (1985) → Girglani Commission (2001–04).

new.s: With respect to the Mulki rules, the Jai Telangana (1969) and Jai Andhra (1972) movements were respectively:
new.x: Telangana in 1969 was for the Mulki rules; Andhra in 1972 was against them.

new.s: In the 1971 Lok Sabha election, the Telangana Praja Samithi won how many of the 14 seats it contested?
new.x: The TPS won 10 of 14 seats.

new.s: Opponents of the TPS merger with the Congress formed the Complete TPS under:
new.x: The Complete TPS was formed under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.

new.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao was sworn in as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on:
new.x: PVNR was sworn in on 30 Sep 1971 after Kasu Brahmananda Reddy resigned.

new.s: Which pair (committee – task under the Eight-Point Formula) is correctly matched?
o: Wanchoo – Legal opinion on job safeguards
new.x: Wanchoo gave legal opinion on job safeguards; Bhargava examined revenue surpluses and Lalit did the official accounting.

new.s: Which committee under the Eight-Point Formula examined Telangana's revenue surpluses?
new.x: Justice Vashist Bhargava's committee examined the revenue surpluses.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT an alleged violation behind the 1969 Telangana agitation?
o: Repeal of the Mulki rules by the 32nd Amendment
Recruitment of non-locals to Telangana posts
Reclassification of local posts as state cadre
new.x: The 32nd Amendment came only in 1973; the others were the alleged violations behind 1969.

new.s: Which case of October 1972 upheld the old Mulki Rules as valid and in force?
o: A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of AP
Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
new.x: Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy (Oct 1972) upheld the Mulki Rules and triggered Jai Andhra.

new.s: After the Six-Point Formula, the Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved on:
new.x: The TRC was dissolved on 1 January 1974.

new.s: The Five-Point Formula on the Mulki rules was announced on:
new.x: The Five-Point Formula came on 27 November 1972.

new.s: Under the Five-Point Formula, the Mulki rules were to continue in the twin cities till:
new.x: Mulki rules were to stay in the twin cities till 1977 and in Telangana till 1980.

new.s: How long did the President's Rule of 1973 in Andhra Pradesh last?
new.x: It ran from 18 January to 10 December 1973, about 11 months.

new.s: The Jai Andhra agitation was called off on:
new.x: After the Six-Point Formula (21 Sep 1973), the agitation was called off on 1 October 1973.

new.s: Which Congress leader, besides Kakani Venkataratnam, was in the Jai Andhra movement?
new.x: B.V. Subba Reddy was a Congress leader in the movement.

new.s: The 32nd Constitutional Amendment came into force on:
new.x: The 32nd Amendment came into force on 1 July 1974.

new.s: The Six-Point Formula, given by the Centre on 21 September 1973, was approved on:
new.x: It was approved on 18 December 1973.

new.s: Under the 1975 Presidential Order, Zone II comprised:
o: East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna
new.x: Zone II was East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone IV was Rayalaseema and Zone VI included Hyderabad.

new.s: The Girglani Commission was set up in 2001 by the government of:
new.x: Naidu set it up in 2001; GO 610 was NTR's (1985).

new.s: The Girglani Commission found large-scale violations especially in:
new.x: Its 2004 report found large-scale violations, especially in Zone VI.

new.s: Under the AP Public Employment Order-2025, Andhra Pradesh has:
new.x: The 2025 Order provides 6 zones and 2 multi-zones.

new.s: The Million March at Tank Bund took place in:
new.x: The Million March was in March 2011.

new.s: The CWC resolution for Telangana was passed in:
new.x: The CWC resolved for Telangana in July 2013.

new.s: The Srikrishna Committee submitted its report on:
new.x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna's committee reported on 30 December 2010 with six options.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha on:
new.x: Lok Sabha 18 Feb, Rajya Sabha 20 Feb 2014.

new.s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided an expert committee for Andhra Pradesh's new capital?
new.x: Section 6 provided the expert committee; Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital.

new.s: Under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 was Polavaram declared a national project?
new.x: Section 90 deals with the Polavaram national project.

new.s: Under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, Andhra Pradesh's Assembly seats were to rise from 175 to:
new.x: Delimitation was to raise AP from 175 to 225 and Telangana from 119 to 153.

new.s: Section 46 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with:
o: Splitting the Finance Commission award and a backward-area package
new.x: Section 46 covers the Finance Commission award split and the backward-area package.

new.s: Under Section 50 of the AP Reorganisation Act, tax arrears are apportioned by:
new.x: Section 50: arrears by place of assessment; Section 56: refunds by population.

new.s: Under Sections 30–31 of the AP Reorganisation Act, the common High Court sat at:
new.x: The common High Court sat at Hyderabad until AP got its own High Court.

new.s: How many Legislative Council seats were allocated to Telangana?
new.x: Telangana got 40 Council seats; AP has 58.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's Legislative Council strength was raised from 50 to 58 by the:
new.x: The 2015 Amendment Act raised it to 58.

new.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, power was apportioned on the basis of:
o: Average consumption of the previous 5 years
new.x: Power was shared by average consumption of the previous five years.

new.s: Which pair (Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act – contents) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Ninth Schedule lists PSUs and corporations; the railway zone is in the Thirteenth.

new.s: Who chaired the Expert Committee on Andhra Pradesh's new capital under Section 6?
new.x: K.C. Sivaramakrishnan chaired it (report Aug 2014).

new.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 amended which Section to move Khammam submergence villages to Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: The Ordinance amended Section 3.

new.s: The Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari waters is chaired by the:
new.x: The Union Water Resources Minister chairs it, with both CMs.

new.s: The AP High Court upheld Amaravati as capital against the three-capitals plan on:
new.x: The AP High Court upheld Amaravati on 3 March 2022.
